world.title: Suspected unexploded Hezbollah munition kills Israeli student, injures 24 near Lebanon border
world.summary: A suspected unexploded munition killed a 15-year-old student and injured 24 people when it detonated during a school hike on Oct. 12 near Neot Mordechai in northern Israel, close to the Lebanon border. The group included students and staff from a religious high school in Ma’alot-Tarshiha; two 14-year-olds were reported
world.content: A suspected unexploded munition killed a 15-year-old student and injured 24 people when it detonated during a school hike on Oct. 12 near Neot Mordechai in northern Israel, close to the Lebanon border. The group included students and staff from a religious high school in Ma’alot-Tarshiha; two 14-year-olds were reported in serious condition. Israeli police and the military said the blast likely involved old Hezbollah ordnance, possibly a cluster munition; police said a student may have been holding it when it exploded. Cluster munitions can leave small explosive charges that fail to detonate on impact and remain dangerous long after fighting ends. The school outing had received official approval, and police are investigating how the munition reached the site and what caused it to detonate. Bomb-disposal experts were sent to secure the area, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the military to reinforce warnings against touching unexploded ordnance.

world.title: Storms kill five in Mexico as Simon threatens Pacific coast
world.summary: Hurricane Simon and the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel have killed at least five people in Mexico, flooded Pacific-coast communities and left people missing, authorities said Monday. Rachel killed four members of one family near Ensenada, Baja California, while a 71-year-old man died when a wall collapsed in Chilpan
world.content: Hurricane Simon and the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel have killed at least five people in Mexico, flooded Pacific-coast communities and left people missing, authorities said Monday. Rachel killed four members of one family near Ensenada, Baja California, while a 71-year-old man died when a wall collapsed in Chilpancingo, Guerrero. At least six people remained missing in Baja California, according to the latest detailed count, and Mexican military helicopters rescued 32 people from a ranch near Ensenada. Simon was a Category 2 hurricane with sustained winds of up to 155 kph late Monday. Although its center remained offshore, the storm brought down trees and power lines, blocked roads and flooded homes, including in Acapulco. Forecasters warned of further flooding and landslides. Authorities warned of dangerous surf and heavy rain, and forecasters said Simon could approach or make landfall on Mexico’s west-central coast later in the week. Baja California officials said about 14,000 federal and state personnel had been deployed and more than 50 people were receiving assistance in temporary shelters. Puerto Vallarta’s international airport suspended operations until Tuesday morning, and authorities urged residents in several states to stay sheltered and avoid road travel.
world.image_alt: Storms kill five in Mexico as Simon threatens Pacific coast

world.title: US economists Hall and Woodford win Nobel for stabilization models
world.summary: American economists Robert E. Hall of Stanford University and Michael Woodford of Columbia University jointly won the 2026 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for research on the “microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation,” the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced Monday in Stockholm. The aw
world.content: American economists Robert E. Hall of Stanford University and Michael Woodford of Columbia University jointly won the 2026 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for research on the “microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation,” the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced Monday in Stockholm. The award is worth 12 million Swedish kronor, reported as about $1.2 million. The economists’ separate work linked household and business decisions to economy-wide fluctuations, giving policymakers models to assess how fiscal and monetary measures can limit damaging swings. The Nobel committee said the research provides a theoretical basis for models used by central banks and governments to analyze shocks such as energy crises or sudden changes in household consumption. Hall examined how consumers decide to save and spend, while Woodford’s research helped apply macroeconomic analysis to central-bank policy, including the use of guidance to influence expectations. The formal prize ceremony is scheduled for Dec. 10 in Stockholm.
world.image_alt: US economists Hall and Woodford win Nobel for stabilization models

world.title: Trump says Putin wants Ukraine deal more than Zelenskyy
world.summary: President Donald Trump said Monday that Russian President Vladimir Putin wants a deal to end the war in Ukraine more than Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy does. He also asserted that both governments had agreed to halt attacks on energy infrastructure. Neither Moscow nor Kyiv had confirmed such an agreement. Tru
world.content: President Donald Trump said Monday that Russian President Vladimir Putin wants a deal to end the war in Ukraine more than Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy does. He also asserted that both governments had agreed to halt attacks on energy infrastructure. Neither Moscow nor Kyiv had confirmed such an agreement. Trump said he would review reports of violations but claimed both sides had breached it. Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to stop striking Russian energy facilities if Russia did the same and asked Washington to take “concrete steps” to enforce the proposal. He said Russia struck a power plant in Kharkiv after Trump’s announcement, further damaging Ukraine’s energy system. Russian drones also continued to attack Kyiv, Zelenskyy said. Trump’s comments followed a US arrangement to temporarily ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports, which he defended as a way to support fuel supplies and lower prices. US and European critics say the deal could benefit Moscow while its invasion continues. Republican senators also challenged its legality under the 2022 congressional ban on Russian energy imports. The Kremlin said contacts with Washington were continuing but did not confirm an energy truce.
world.image_alt: Trump says Putin wants Ukraine deal more than Zelenskyy

world.title: IMF lifts 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1%, flags risks
world.summary: The International Monetary Fund raised its forecast for global economic growth in 2026 to 3.1% from 3.0% in July, but warned of risks from war-driven energy costs, rising debt and financial risks linked to artificial intelligence. The Fund expects growth to slow from 3.5% in 2025 before reaching 3.4% in 2027. Its proje
world.content: The International Monetary Fund raised its forecast for global economic growth in 2026 to 3.1% from 3.0% in July, but warned of risks from war-driven energy costs, rising debt and financial risks linked to artificial intelligence. The Fund expects growth to slow from 3.5% in 2025 before reaching 3.4% in 2027. Its projections assume oil and gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz resume by March and AI demand moderates. The IMF said AI investment is helping offset the effects of higher energy prices. Growth is also increasingly concentrated: 32 economies now account for 95% of global growth, compared with 54 in April. The Fund expects growth in developing economies and emerging markets to slow to 3.7% this year from 4.5% in 2025, with energy-importing low-income countries particularly exposed. Other risks include a possible correction in AI-related stock prices, rising bond yields and cyberthreats that could disrupt financial systems, IMF officials said. The Fund forecasts global inflation will rise to 4.7% this year as oil prices average about $96 a barrel, then ease to 4.1% in 2027.
world.image_alt: IMF lifts 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1%, flags risks

world.title: Houthi official threatens U.S. interests if Washington joins Yemen war
world.summary: A senior Houthi official warned Monday that the group would strike the United States and its interests in the region if Washington joined Saudi Arabia’s military campaign in Yemen. He also told workers to stay away from Saudi oil facilities and airports. President Donald Trump said he was considering joining Saudi stri
world.content: A senior Houthi official warned Monday that the group would strike the United States and its interests in the region if Washington joined Saudi Arabia’s military campaign in Yemen. He also told workers to stay away from Saudi oil facilities and airports. President Donald Trump said he was considering joining Saudi strikes after attacks on the kingdom, including Saturday’s attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport. Saudi authorities reported 12 deaths and 309 injuries; other accounts put the death toll at 13. The warning followed renewed fighting in Yemen and repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi transport and energy infrastructure. On Monday night, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile over Riyadh and two ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait. The Houthis also claimed another attack on the airport. Riyadh’s airport remained closed while authorities conducted safety checks, with no reopening date announced. Airlines suspended or changed services, and the U.S. Embassy required government staff to obtain approval before using any airport in Saudi Arabia. Fighting between the Houthis and Yemen’s internationally recognized government, backed by a Saudi-led coalition, resumed in July. Riyadh has led the coalition since 2015.
world.image_alt: Houthi official threatens U.S. interests if Washington joins Yemen war

world.title: Indian youth protest group reports new arrests as voter-roll case reaches court
world.summary: India’s Cockroach Janta Party said police detained three of its leaders and other members early Tuesday as they tried to reach Jantar Mantar, a day after opposition parties marched to the Supreme Court and filed a joint petition challenging the nationwide voter-roll revision. The protest group had sought permission to
world.content: India’s Cockroach Janta Party said police detained three of its leaders and other members early Tuesday as they tried to reach Jantar Mantar, a day after opposition parties marched to the Supreme Court and filed a joint petition challenging the nationwide voter-roll revision. The protest group had sought permission to demonstrate at Jantar Mantar, which Delhi Police removed from its list of designated protest sites on Monday. The petition, signed by opposition figures including Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, seeks an audit of deleted voter registrations, protections against removals without notice or a hearing, and a temporary nationwide halt to the revision. The Supreme Court was expected to hear it on Tuesday, Oct. 13. Chief Justice Surya Kant had earlier declined the opposition’s request for a meeting, saying the issue should be pursued through court proceedings. The review, which began last year, has removed more than 130 million names. Election authorities say the removals target duplicate registrations and deceased or untraceable registrants, while opposition parties allege the process could disenfranchise eligible voters and benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s BJP. Both the Election Commission and BJP reject claims of manipulation.
world.image_alt: Indian youth protest group reports new arrests as voter-roll case reaches court

world.title: Russia strikes six Ukrainian energy sites after Trump ceasefire claim
world.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russian forces struck six energy facilities on Monday, Oct. 12, after President Donald Trump declared an immediate halt to attacks on energy infrastructure. Zelenskyy reported 33 people wounded nationwide. The strikes hit a gas production facility and energy sites in several
world.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russian forces struck six energy facilities on Monday, Oct. 12, after President Donald Trump declared an immediate halt to attacks on energy infrastructure. Zelenskyy reported 33 people wounded nationwide. The strikes hit a gas production facility and energy sites in several regions, causing damage that prompted power cuts in Kharkiv, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia. Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed because he told them they had, but acknowledged violations on both sides. Moscow has not confirmed the arrangement, and Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said Zelenskyy did not deserve a respite. Zelenskyy said Ukraine had not attacked Russian refineries overnight and was ready to formalize a reciprocal pause, but warned that Kyiv would respond if Russia continued its strikes. Ukrainian and European officials told CBS the Trump administration had threatened to halt intelligence sharing and European purchases of U.S. weapons for Ukraine through the PURL system unless Kyiv stopped deep strikes on Russian energy sites. The European Union added about 1,569 people and businesses to its Russia sanctions list, its largest expansion since the 2022 invasion. Kyiv said it was waiting for details of U.S.-Russia contacts.
world.image_alt: Russia strikes six Ukrainian energy sites after Trump ceasefire claim

business.title: Buyers gain housing leverage, but mortgage rates near 7% deter purchases
business.summary: In many parts of the United States, housing conditions have shifted toward buyers, but mortgage rates around 7% are keeping many prospective buyers on the sidelines. The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage reached 7.4% earlier in October, affecting buyers, sellers and some recent homeowners. Affordability pre
business.content: In many parts of the United States, housing conditions have shifted toward buyers, but mortgage rates around 7% are keeping many prospective buyers on the sidelines. The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage reached 7.4% earlier in October, affecting buyers, sellers and some recent homeowners. Affordability pressures are also spreading into the Midwest. Redfin projections cited by Fox Business suggest housing costs could take five to 10 years to return to more typical levels; a Business Insider headline cited in the same report says many Americans may not be able to afford a home until 2031. Buyers have more negotiating power in some areas, but elevated borrowing costs limit how many can purchase a home.
business.image_alt: Buyers gain housing leverage, but mortgage rates near 7% deter purchases

business.title: India inflation hits 5.54% as food prices fuel rate-hike debate
business.summary: India’s retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September from 4.83% in August, exceeding economists’ estimates, as food inflation accelerated to 7.74%. Inflation exceeded the Reserve Bank of India’s 4% target but remained within its 2%-6% tolerance band. Food prices drove much of the rise: onion inflation more than doubled
business.content: India’s retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September from 4.83% in August, exceeding economists’ estimates, as food inflation accelerated to 7.74%. Inflation exceeded the Reserve Bank of India’s 4% target but remained within its 2%-6% tolerance band. Food prices drove much of the rise: onion inflation more than doubled to 108.09%, while garlic and lemon inflation also climbed. The figures followed a recent RBI rate hike and renewed expectations of another increase. DBS Bank economist Radhika Rao said the central bank could consider a December hike as food, fuel and services pressures build.
business.image_alt: India inflation hits 5.54% as food prices fuel rate-hike debate

business.title: Hackers overheat French supermarket fridges, spoiling food across hundreds of stores
business.summary: Cyberattackers manipulated connected refrigeration controls at hundreds of French supermarkets overnight into Monday, heating some units to 50C for six hours and prompting retailers to discard fresh and frozen food. Retailers put the number of affected stores at about 400; Danish engineering firm Danfoss supplied the c
business.content: Cyberattackers manipulated connected refrigeration controls at hundreds of French supermarkets overnight into Monday, heating some units to 50C for six hours and prompting retailers to discard fresh and frozen food. Retailers put the number of affected stores at about 400; Danish engineering firm Danfoss supplied the compromised systems. Some locations also reported fires, while two supermarkets in Alsace reported combined losses of €270,000. Paris prosecutors opened a cybercrime investigation, and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu directed France’s cybersecurity agency, ANSSI, to investigate and coordinate with European counterparts. Intermarché chief executive Thierry Cotillard estimated the attack could cost tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day. The full extent of the damage and who carried out the attack remain unclear.
business.image_alt: Hackers overheat French supermarket fridges, spoiling food across hundreds of stores

business.title: Starbucks rules out Chipotle takeover after report of possible record deal
business.summary: Starbucks said Monday it is not buying Chipotle Mexican Grill after the Financial Times reported on Oct. 8 that the coffee chain had consulted advisers in recent months about a possible offer. Chipotle’s market value was around $40 billion, and one analysis estimated that a purchase price could reach about $50 billion
business.content: Starbucks said Monday it is not buying Chipotle Mexican Grill after the Financial Times reported on Oct. 8 that the coffee chain had consulted advisers in recent months about a possible offer. Chipotle’s market value was around $40 billion, and one analysis estimated that a purchase price could reach about $50 billion with a takeover premium, potentially making it the largest restaurant-sector deal on record. Starbucks said it is focused on its “Back to Starbucks” strategy and plans to release fourth-quarter results and fiscal 2027 guidance later this month. The speculation linked Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol to the burrito chain he led for six years before joining Starbucks in 2024. Analysts questioned the rationale for a deal while Starbucks pursues a turnaround; one adviser said financing a premium bid with debt and new shares could increase leverage and dilute shareholders.
business.image_alt: Starbucks rules out Chipotle takeover after report of possible record deal

business.title: Three tech giants now account for 22% of S&P 500 market value
business.summary: The S&P 500 hit another record on Monday as its four-year bull market continued, even though about four in 10 stocks in the index were down for the year. Gains have become concentrated in a few companies: Apple, Microsoft and Nvidia together account for about 22% of the index’s market value, up from roughly 14% in late
business.content: The S&P 500 hit another record on Monday as its four-year bull market continued, even though about four in 10 stocks in the index were down for the year. Gains have become concentrated in a few companies: Apple, Microsoft and Nvidia together account for about 22% of the index’s market value, up from roughly 14% in late 2022. Market breadth—the share of stocks rising or falling—was at a record low for a day when the index hit a record, according to Ned Davis Research. The Kobeissi Letter found that 84% of S&P 500 companies were at least 10% below their all-time highs. It also said a group of 42 AI stocks generated 67% of the index’s price return since the start of 2024.
business.image_alt: Three tech giants now account for 22% of S&P 500 market value

business.title: Microsoft president urges enforceable global rules for AI safety
business.summary: Microsoft President Brad Smith called for enforceable global safety rules for artificial intelligence, including mandatory incident reporting, notifications to people harmed by rogue AI agents and emergency controls that can pause or slow systems. He said AI faces fewer safety requirements than everyday products such a
business.content: Microsoft President Brad Smith called for enforceable global safety rules for artificial intelligence, including mandatory incident reporting, notifications to people harmed by rogue AI agents and emergency controls that can pause or slow systems. He said AI faces fewer safety requirements than everyday products such as milk and washing machines and argued that independent evaluators should assess some systems before release. Smith’s proposal goes beyond a voluntary agreement that major technology companies signed at a White House meeting in September. He said voluntary commitments cannot ensure that less responsible developers follow safety practices. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has also called for an emergency brake on advanced AI. Smith pointed to the UK’s AI Security Institute as a potential source of technical leadership. UK AI minister Kanishka Narayan was due to urge frontier-model developers to strengthen safeguards, and the government was preparing legislation to increase oversight, the Guardian reported.
business.image_alt: Microsoft president urges enforceable global rules for AI safety

business.title: South Korea’s Kospi slides 5.46% as AI chip concerns spread
business.summary: South Korea’s Kospi fell 5.46% to close at 6,035.35 on Tuesday, extending its losing streak to five sessions after dropping more than 7% intraday. Samsung Electronics lost 7.39% and SK Hynix fell 10.09% as chip shares led the selloff. Investors weighed signs of stronger Chinese competition after memory-chip maker CXMT
business.content: South Korea’s Kospi fell 5.46% to close at 6,035.35 on Tuesday, extending its losing streak to five sessions after dropping more than 7% intraday. Samsung Electronics lost 7.39% and SK Hynix fell 10.09% as chip shares led the selloff. Investors weighed signs of stronger Chinese competition after memory-chip maker CXMT said it had developed technology to pack more data onto chips and planned a server-memory product by year-end. CXMT has not demonstrated that it can produce chips using the technology at scale. Its announcement does not immediately threaten South Korea’s lead in high-bandwidth memory, but it added to concerns about chipmakers’ pricing power. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan also warned that financing, rather than chips or electricity, could constrain AI expansion. Investors were awaiting the U.S. consumer price index report due Wednesday for clues on Federal Reserve policy.
business.image_alt: South Korea’s Kospi slides 5.46% as AI chip concerns spread

science.title: Migraine drug study links CGRP blockers to higher miscarriage risk
science.summary: An observational study of 7,579 pregnancies found that exposure to CGRP-targeting migraine drugs was associated with about a 40% higher risk of miscarriage in the first 20 weeks of pregnancy compared with periods without exposure. The drugs block a peptide involved in migraine attacks that also plays a role in blood fl
science.content: An observational study of 7,579 pregnancies found that exposure to CGRP-targeting migraine drugs was associated with about a 40% higher risk of miscarriage in the first 20 weeks of pregnancy compared with periods without exposure. The drugs block a peptide involved in migraine attacks that also plays a role in blood flow, embryo implantation and placental development. The study used U.S. insurance records from 2018 to 2021 and cannot establish that the medicines caused the pregnancy losses. Researchers called for more research on miscarriage, fetal outcomes and longer-term effects on children. Propranolol exposure was not associated with increased risk in the analysis.
science.image_alt: Migraine drug study links CGRP blockers to higher miscarriage risk

science.title: Australian researchers film how detached bee stingers keep pumping venom
science.summary: Australian researchers have filmed how a honeybee’s detached stinger continues injecting venom, showing that two valves inside the roughly 2-millimetre stinger act as opposing, collapsible pistons. High-speed video showed the valves alternately sealing and collapsing as they move, allowing the stinger to keep pumping a
science.content: Australian researchers have filmed how a honeybee’s detached stinger continues injecting venom, showing that two valves inside the roughly 2-millimetre stinger act as opposing, collapsible pistons. High-speed video showed the valves alternately sealing and collapsing as they move, allowing the stinger to keep pumping after it separates from the bee. The study, by researchers from Macquarie University and the University of New South Wales, appeared in PNAS. The team used scans and a 3D-printed model to test the mechanism. The researchers say the design could inform small pumps for drug delivery, including insulin, but those uses have not been demonstrated.
science.image_alt: Australian researchers film how detached bee stingers keep pumping venom

science.title: Taurid meteor showers to peak on two dark November nights
science.summary: The Southern and Northern Taurid meteor showers are expected to peak on separate November nights and can produce occasional bright, slow-moving fireballs visible worldwide. The Southern shower’s fireball-associated component peaks overnight Nov. 4-5, while the Northern Taurids peak Nov. 11-12. The showers overlap in la
science.content: The Southern and Northern Taurid meteor showers are expected to peak on separate November nights and can produce occasional bright, slow-moving fireballs visible worldwide. The Southern shower’s fireball-associated component peaks overnight Nov. 4-5, while the Northern Taurids peak Nov. 11-12. The showers overlap in late October and early November. Moonlight is expected to be limited during both peak periods, with a waning crescent for the Southern peak and a 5%-lit crescent for the Northern peak. The American Meteor Society lists the Southern Taurids as active through Nov. 20 and the Northern Taurids through Dec. 10.
science.image_alt: Taurid meteor showers to peak on two dark November nights

science.title: Elephant carcasses leave nutrient legacies that reshape savanna ecosystems
science.summary: A study reports that nutrients left by elephant carcasses create areas of lower biodiversity alongside hotspots of ecosystem processes. The research examines elephants’ ecological influence after death, beyond their effects while alive. Elephants shape African savannas by consuming large amounts of forage, digging for
science.content: A study reports that nutrients left by elephant carcasses create areas of lower biodiversity alongside hotspots of ecosystem processes. The research examines elephants’ ecological influence after death, beyond their effects while alive. Elephants shape African savannas by consuming large amounts of forage, digging for water and knocking down trees, affecting other animals. The findings describe distinct ecological effects around elephant remains.
science.image_alt: Elephant carcasses leave nutrient legacies that reshape savanna ecosystems

science.title: IPCC nations deadlock over timetable for next climate reports
science.summary: Member countries of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change have not agreed on a timetable for its next assessment reports at a meeting in Addis Ababa, with the dispute focused on when to publish its mitigation report. India, Kenya, Saudi Arabia, Russia and China are pressing for more preparation time, saying sci
science.content: Member countries of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change have not agreed on a timetable for its next assessment reports at a meeting in Addis Ababa, with the dispute focused on when to publish its mitigation report. India, Kenya, Saudi Arabia, Russia and China are pressing for more preparation time, saying scientists from less-resourced countries need a meaningful chance to contribute. Piers Forster, a climate scientist and former IPCC report author, says most governments want the three parts of the current assessment completed by the end of 2028 so they can inform the next Global Stocktake under the Paris Agreement. He argues that publishing the mitigation report after the stocktake could delay discussion of stronger emissions cuts. The IPCC is meeting this week.
science.image_alt: IPCC nations deadlock over timetable for next climate reports

science.title: Model predicts outer planets’ orbits could become unstable in about one billion years
science.summary: The Sun’s mass loss could destabilize some outer planets’ orbits roughly one billion years from now, according to a model—far sooner than the previous estimate of about a quintillion years.
science.content: The Sun’s mass loss could destabilize some outer planets’ orbits roughly one billion years from now, according to a model—far sooner than the previous estimate of about a quintillion years.

science.title: NASA selects rover mission to investigate Moon’s Marius Hills pit
science.summary: NASA has selected the GIMLI mission to investigate whether the Marius Hills pit on the Moon opens into an underground lava tube, a structure that could reveal details of lunar volcanism and offer shelter for future astronauts. The pit has been observed from orbit, but GIMLI would use a rover to study it from the lunar
science.content: NASA has selected the GIMLI mission to investigate whether the Marius Hills pit on the Moon opens into an underground lava tube, a structure that could reveal details of lunar volcanism and offer shelter for future astronauts. The pit has been observed from orbit, but GIMLI would use a rover to study it from the lunar surface. The rover is expected to carry ground-penetrating radar, seismic probes, a gravimeter and cameras to assess whether a larger cavity lies beneath the opening. NASA is funding the project through its PRISM program; Honeybee Robotics is helping build the instruments, and a commercial lunar lander is planned to deliver the mission under the CLPS program.
science.image_alt: NASA selects rover mission to investigate Moon’s Marius Hills pit

science.title: Large menopause study finds abrupt shifts across multiple body systems
science.summary: An analysis of more than 300 million clinical tests from over one million women found abrupt shifts across multiple body systems around the final menstrual period, challenging the view that menopause-related changes are simply gradual aging. In the U.S. data, 52 of 90 laboratory measures changed significantly and abrup
science.content: An analysis of more than 300 million clinical tests from over one million women found abrupt shifts across multiple body systems around the final menstrual period, challenging the view that menopause-related changes are simply gradual aging. In the U.S. data, 52 of 90 laboratory measures changed significantly and abruptly, including measures of bone metabolism, liver and kidney function, blood chemistry and lipids. Men of comparable age showed no equivalent abrupt pattern. Reproductive hormone changes began earlier: anti-Müllerian hormone and estradiol declined, while follicle-stimulating hormone rose. These shifts were detectable roughly 12 to 15 years before the final period. Women using menopausal hormone therapy showed smaller changes, but the study does not establish that the treatment prevents chronic disease. The researchers analyzed U.S. and Israeli cohorts using a method that separates chronological age from reproductive timing.
science.image_alt: Large menopause study finds abrupt shifts across multiple body systems

sports.title: Saracens dismiss 21-year-old academy forward after St Albans incident
sports.summary: Saracens dismissed academy forward Totoa Auvaa with immediate effect on Monday, 12 October, after an internal investigation into an off-field incident in St Albans over the weekend. Hertfordshire police are investigating an alleged assault in the early hours of Sunday, 11 October. They say a man in his 20s was approach
sports.content: Saracens dismissed academy forward Totoa Auvaa with immediate effect on Monday, 12 October, after an internal investigation into an off-field incident in St Albans over the weekend. Hertfordshire police are investigating an alleged assault in the early hours of Sunday, 11 October. They say a man in his 20s was approached and punched in the face. Saracens said Auvaa’s conduct fell short of the standards expected of people representing the club and said it would make no further comment. The dismissal follows a June nightclub incident involving England cricketers Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson. Auvaa aimed a punch at Atkinson that missed and struck an ECB security guard, who needed stitches; Saracens took no disciplinary action at the time. Stokes and Atkinson missed England’s second Test against New Zealand, although an ECB hearing found them blameless for violent conduct. Police inquiries into the St Albans allegation are ongoing.
sports.image_alt: Saracens dismiss 21-year-old academy forward after St Albans incident

sports.title: Ronaldo scores as Al-Nassr win after Riyadh missile alert
sports.summary: Al-Nassr beat Uzbekistan’s Neftchi Fergana 3-1 in the AFC Champions League Elite on Monday after a security alert delayed kick-off in Riyadh by about an hour. Cristiano Ronaldo scored the Saudi club’s second goal, taking his career tally to 981, as Al-Nassr secured their first win in this season’s competition. Saudi Ci
sports.content: Al-Nassr beat Uzbekistan’s Neftchi Fergana 3-1 in the AFC Champions League Elite on Monday after a security alert delayed kick-off in Riyadh by about an hour. Cristiano Ronaldo scored the Saudi club’s second goal, taking his career tally to 981, as Al-Nassr secured their first win in this season’s competition. Saudi Civil Defence issued a warning 15 minutes before the scheduled start, and the Saudi-led military coalition later said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired toward the capital by Yemen’s Houthis. The stadium announcer told spectators the situation was safe and asked them to remain in their seats; the match eventually went ahead. Angelo opened the scoring in the 33rd minute, Ronaldo made it 2-0 before half-time, and Neftchi’s Alisher Odilov pulled one back early in the second half. Neftchi were reduced to 10 men in the 65th minute, and Anvarjon Gofurov’s own goal sealed the result. Al-Nassr had lost 4-0 to Al-Ain in their opening match.
sports.image_alt: Ronaldo scores as Al-Nassr win after Riyadh missile alert

sports.title: Eagles’ Sirianni takes blame for late-game error in London loss
sports.summary: Philadelphia coach Nick Sirianni took responsibility for a late kickoff decision after the Eagles lost 19-17 to Jacksonville in London on Cam Little’s 57-yard game-winning field goal. Philadelphia had taken a 17-16 lead with eight seconds left, but Ameer Abdullah returned the ensuing kick 53 yards; Sirianni said he sho
sports.content: Philadelphia coach Nick Sirianni took responsibility for a late kickoff decision after the Eagles lost 19-17 to Jacksonville in London on Cam Little’s 57-yard game-winning field goal. Philadelphia had taken a 17-16 lead with eight seconds left, but Ameer Abdullah returned the ensuing kick 53 yards; Sirianni said he should have chosen a different approach. The loss dropped the Eagles to 2-3 and extended their losing streak to three games. Washington coach Dan Quinn also took responsibility after the Commanders and New York Giants tied 27-27. Washington reached field-goal range in overtime but ran out of time without attempting a potential game-winning kick. Philadelphia, Washington and Dallas all lost or tied in Week 5.

sports.content: The Cleveland Guardians scored seven runs over the final four innings to beat the Tampa Bay Rays 7-3 in Monday’s American League Championship Series opener at Tropicana Field, taking a 1-0 lead in the best-of-seven series. Nathaniel Lowe broke a 2-2 tie with a two-run single in the eighth, and José Ramírez and Jo Adell added runs in the ninth. Cleveland trailed 2-0 after Tampa Bay scored twice in the first. Chase DeLauter homered in the sixth and Patrick Bailey tied the game with a solo home run in the seventh, both off Rays starter Drew Rasmussen; the Guardians then scored against Tampa Bay’s bullpen. The win was Cleveland’s fourth straight in the postseason, following a comeback from a 2-0 series deficit against the White Sox in the Division Series. Game 2 is scheduled for Tuesday, Oct. 13, at Tropicana Field, with rookie left-hander Parker Messick starting for Cleveland against Tampa Bay right-hander Freddy Peralta.

sports.content: Arsenal will be without Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi for Tuesday’s Champions League match against Lille after both suffered ankle injuries in a training session following Saturday’s 2-1 win over Leeds. Manager Mikel Arteta said Hincapie’s injury appeared more serious, but scans were needed to determine how long either player would be out. The pair were taking part in a small-sided session for players who had limited playing time against Leeds. The session was intended to maintain match fitness while the rest of the squad had a recovery day. Arteta said he would not abandon the routine, arguing that without extra work, reserve players could lack rhythm when called upon. He described the injuries as freak occurrences in a contact sport. Arsenal expected to learn more after further scans on Monday. William Saliba had resumed individual work on the grass as he recovered from a back injury, and Arteta said the club hoped he would return to team training in the coming weeks.

sports.content: Coventry City beat Newcastle United 4-1 at home on Monday, winning a second successive Premier League match and moving out of the relegation zone. Jack Rudoni opened the scoring from the penalty spot after goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek brought down Sidiki Cherif. Cherif doubled the lead early in the second half before Sven Botman pulled a goal back for Newcastle with a long-range strike. Substitute Ellis Simms restored Coventry’s two-goal lead, and 18-year-old Stephen Mfuni completed the scoring. The result lifted Frank Lampard’s newly promoted side from 19th to 14th on six points, while Newcastle remained 11th with eight. It was Coventry’s first home top-flight victory in 25 years. The club began the season with four defeats without scoring before winning 1-0 at Nottingham Forest and then beating Newcastle. Newcastle had chances to equalize before the break, but Coventry defender Bobby Thomas twice cleared efforts off the line. Coventry next visit Tottenham on October 19, while Newcastle host Aston Villa on Saturday.

sports.content: Milwaukee beat Los Angeles 7-4 in Game 2 of the National League Championship Series on Monday, taking a 2-0 lead as the best-of-seven series heads to Dodger Stadium. William Contreras tied the game with a fifth-inning homer and singled home the go-ahead run in the sixth. He finished 3-for-4 with three RBIs. The Dodgers led three times but managed only three hits, while Milwaukee’s relievers retired the final 15 batters after starter Logan Henderson exited early. Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched 2⅔ innings for Los Angeles, his shortest postseason start, and allowed three earned runs. Los Angeles will discuss whether to sit Shohei Ohtani for Wednesday’s Game 3. Manager Dave Roberts said Ohtani does not feel well, and no decision has been made. The Dodgers are scheduled to start Blake Snell against Milwaukee’s Robert Gasser, with Games 3, 4 and, if needed, 5 all set for Los Angeles.

sports.content: Alexander Zverev is guaranteed to finish 2026 as the men’s year-end world No. 1 after Carlos Alcaraz lost 7-5, 7-6 (7-4) to Belgium’s Zizou Bergs in the third round of the Shanghai Masters on Monday, October 12. Zverev becomes the first German man to finish a season at No. 1 and the oldest player to claim the year-end honour for the first time. Zverev, currently ranked second, won his first Grand Slam title at the French Open in June and added the US Open title in September. Jannik Sinner, still the current No. 1, ended his season with a knee injury, while Alcaraz had been sidelined for nearly five months with a wrist injury. Zverev won both majors without facing either rival, BBC Sport reported. Zverev can take over the live No. 1 ranking as early as November 2, but his year-end position is already assured; the final season ranking is due November 23. He remains in Shanghai, where he was set to face Alexander Bublik in the next round.
